acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Donated to the Rockefeller Archive Center via the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, in accordance with the terms of access to the RBF collection.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Beginning in 1939, Dana S. Creel served as an assistant to Arthur Packard, who was a long-time associate and financial advisor of John D. Rockefeller, Jr, and directed the philanthropic activities of Room 5600, the Rockefeller family office.
Creel served in the Army during WWII primarily in a counterintelligence unit in Asia. During his military service, he developed what became a lifelong friendship with David Rockefeller.
Creel was appointed Director of the Rockefeller Brothers Fund in 1950, and served as the Fund's first President from 1968-1975, at which time he continued his service to the RBF as a trustee.

Upon his 1950 appointment, Creel was the first professional staff at RBF reponsible for overseeing operations, distinct from the personal giving of Rockefeller family members through the Fund or otherwise through the activities of Room 5600. During his time at RBF, the Fund drastically expanded it's staff and the scope and breadth of it's programatic activites.

As an RBF trustee in 1975-1980, he led the Creel Committee in a reassessment of financial support for the Fund and its long-term committments, which helped provide financial flexibility to explore programmitic and institutional expansion and position the Fund for the next generation of philanthropic giving.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Dana Creel papers chronicle his service to, and membership on the Board of Directors and/or Board of Trustees of, the Interchurch Center, the Martha Baird Rockefeller Fund for Music, Sleepy Hollow Restorations, and the Governing Council of the Rockefeller Archive Center.

The collection primarily documents the planning, partition, and donation of portions of the Rockefeller family Pocantico Hills, NY estate, Kykuit, as a historic site of the National Trust for Historic Preservation, and the development of the vital cooperative roles played by the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, in the operation and maintenance of the site, and Sleepy Hollow Restorations, later Historic Hudson Valley, in operating the visitation program including public tours of the house and gardens and its collections.

The Creel papers also document the early years of the Rockefeller Archive Center, 1972-1985, including the initial proposal and planning, funding, establishment of the Center as a part of Rockefeller University, and the scope and development of its associated collections, including the archival records of the founding donors the Rockefeller family, Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and Rockefeller Foundation.

Also of interest are several files documenting Rockefeller family donations, including a file of summaries of the philanthropic giving of John D. Rockefeller and John D. Rockefeller, Jr. during the period 1855-1960, and later family donations toward the restoration of Lyndhurst as well as acquistion and maintenance of the Union Church of Pocantico Hills by Sleepy Hollow Restorations.
